summary: Susanne Hoeber Rudolph worked in Indology and related fields after earning degrees at Sarah Lawrence College, Harvard University, and Radcliffe College. She taught political science at Harvard (~1955–1963), served as professor at the University of Chicago (1964), and was APSA president (2003–2004).

Susanne Mrozik specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, holding an M.T.S. from Harvard Divinity School and a PhD from Harvard University, where she studied under Charles Hallisey, Diana L. Eck, Stephanie W. Jamison, and Margaret R. Miles. She held posts at Western Michigan University and Mount Holyoke College.

Sushanta Sen, a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, studied at Visva-Bharati University, where he became a lecturer in 1986. He also served as a lecturer in Indian religions in the Department of Theology at the University of Birmingham.

Indologist Sushil Kumar De studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, SOAS, and the University of Bonn. He held positions at Presidency University (~1913–1917), University of Calcutta (~1917–1923), University of Dhaka (~1923–1947), Jadavpur University (1947), and Sanskrit College (~1951–1956).
Susmita Basu Majumdar works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Lady Brabourne College and the University of Calcutta, where she later held a post around 1999.

Susumu Otake, working in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied at the University of Tsukuba (~1993–2002) under Makio Takemura. He served as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (~2008–2009), Hanazono University (~2008–2014), and Bukkyo University (~2012–2015).

Susumu Shimazono studied at the University of Tokyo and UC Berkeley. A scholar of religious studies and Japanology, he taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo (1987, 1995–2013) before directing an institute at Sophia University (~2013–2021).

Susumu Yamaguchi, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studied at Otani University, the University of Paris, and Kyoto University under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He was long a professor at Otani University (1934–1964).

Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri, active in Buddhist studies, studied at Nalanda College, University of London, University of Pennsylvania, and University of Toronto. He founded and served as president of Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies and held posts at Toronto and Ontario Tech University.

Suzanne Karpelès was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She served at the EFEO, National Library of Cambodia, Buddhist Institute, and the École Supérieure de Pāli.

Suzanne Newcombe works in religious studies and Indology and earned a doctorate from the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at the London School of Economics, University of Cambridge, Inform, Open University, and King's College London.

Sven Hedin studied history/archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology at Stockholm University, Uppsala University, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and Humboldt University of Berlin, studying under Ferdinand von Richthofen (~1889–1892).
Sven Wittemann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under supervisor Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Swami Dayananda Saraswati worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and with Chinmayananda Saraswati, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, Swami Pranavananda, and Swami Tarananda Giri.
Swami Siddheswarananda was active in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras and was affiliated with the Ramakrishna Order from around 1920 to 1957.

Swami Sivananda was an Indian figure in philosophy and religious studies who studied at Thanjavur Medical College (~1905–1910). He founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948.
Swami Vimalananda, who worked in religious studies and philosophy, studied at Ripon College and was a disciple of Swami Vivekananda starting in 1897.
Swami Vishnudevananda worked in religious studies and Indology, studying as a disciple under Swami Sivananda from ~1947 to 1957, and later founded the Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda, a figure in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (~1879–1884), and trained under Ramakrishna (~1881–1886).

Sydney Frank Markham, who worked in history/archaeology and Indology, studied at Wadham College, Oxford (~1920–1923). He served as secretary and then president of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).
